q: She ___ to school every day.
e: Present simple is used for habits and routines.

q: They ___ football now.
e: Present continuous is used for actions happening now.

q: I ___ my homework yesterday.
e: Past simple is used for a finished action in the past.

q: We ___ in Lomé since 2020.
e: Present perfect with 'since' describes a period up to now.

q: She is ___ teacher.
e: 'Teacher' starts with a consonant sound, so we use 'a'.

q: ___ sun rises in the east.
e: We use 'the' for unique things such as the sun.

q: I ___ swim very well.
e: 'Can' expresses ability.

q: You ___ see a doctor. You are very sick.
e: 'Should' gives advice.

q: This book is ___ than that one.
e: Short adjectives add -er in comparisons with 'than'.

q: Maya is ___ girl in the class.
e: Superlatives use 'the' plus -est.

q: The bus leaves ___ 7 o'clock.
e: We use 'at' with clock times.

q: We will meet ___ Monday.
e: We use 'on' with days of the week.

q: We live ___ Togo.
e: We use 'in' with countries.

q: The woman ___ lives next door is a nurse.
e: 'Who' refers to people.

q: This is the shop ___ I buy bread.
e: 'Where' refers to a place.

q: If it rains, we ___ at home.
e: First conditional: 'if' plus present, 'will' plus base verb.

q: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius.
e: Present simple is used for facts.

q: English ___ in many countries.
e: Passive: be plus past participle.

q: The letter ___ yesterday.
e: Passive past simple: was plus past participle.

q: I ___ you a text tomorrow.
e: 'Will' is used for a future decision or promise.

q: If I ___ rich, I would travel the world.
e: Second conditional uses 'were' for all persons in standard English.

q: If she had studied, she ___ the exam.
e: Third conditional describes an imagined past result.

q: You ___ wear a helmet on a motorbike. It is the law.
e: 'Must' expresses obligation or a strict rule.

q: He ___ be at home; his car is outside.
e: 'Must be' expresses a strong logical deduction.

q: The bridge ___ in 1990.
e: Passive past simple: was plus past participle.

q: The homework has ___ by the students.
e: Present perfect passive: has been plus past participle.

q: He said, 'I will call you.' He said he ___ call me.
e: In reported speech, 'will' changes to 'would'.

q: They asked, 'Where is the station?' They asked me where the station ___.
e: Reported questions keep statement word order and move back in tense.

q: The man ___ car was stolen called the police.
e: 'Whose' shows possession in a relative clause.

q: The reason ___ she left is unknown.
e: 'Why' introduces a relative clause after 'the reason'.

q: She is ___ honest person.
e: 'Honest' starts with a vowel sound because the h is silent.

q: I play ___ piano every evening.
e: We use 'the' with musical instruments.

q: He is afraid ___ dogs.
e: The adjective 'afraid' takes 'of'.

q: He is interested ___ music.
e: The adjective 'interested' takes 'in'.

q: Please turn ___ the lights when you leave.
e: 'Turn off' means to stop a light or device working.

q: I must give ___ smoking.
e: 'Give up' means to stop doing something.

q: We had to put ___ the meeting until next week.
e: 'Put off' means to postpone.

q: The more you practise, ___ you become.
e: 'The more... the better' shows that two things increase together.

q: This test is ___ than I expected.
e: Short adjectives take -er in comparatives.

q: By the time I arrived, the film ___.
e: Past perfect shows an action completed before another past action.

q: Had I known about the traffic, I ___ earlier.
e: This is an inverted third conditional without 'if'.

q: Unless you ___ harder, you will fail.
e: 'Unless' means 'if not', so the present simple follows.

q: I wish I ___ more time to study.
e: 'Wish' plus past simple expresses a present regret.

q: They ___ have left already; the house is dark.
e: 'Must have' plus past participle expresses a logical deduction about the past.

q: Passengers ___ show their ticket before boarding.
e: 'Must' expresses a strict obligation.

q: The new hospital is expected ___ next year.
e: Passive infinitive: to be plus past participle.

q: He is believed ___ the country.
e: 'Is believed to have' is the passive reporting structure.

q: The results ___ by the teacher yesterday.
e: Passive past simple with a plural subject uses 'were'.

q: He said, 'I have finished my work.' He said that he ___ finished his work.
e: Present perfect moves back to past perfect in reported speech.

q: She asked me, 'Will you come tomorrow?' She asked me ___ I would come the next day.
e: Yes/no questions become reported with 'if' or 'whether'.

q: The project, ___ was expensive, was cancelled.
e: A non-defining clause about a thing uses 'which', with commas.

q: Mariama, ___ brother is a doctor, lives in Kara.
e: 'Whose' replaces 'her brother' in the relative clause.

q: She works at ___ University of Lomé.
e: We use 'the' with the name of a university with 'of'.

q: She is capable ___ solving the problem.
e: The adjective 'capable' takes 'of'.

q: He is responsible ___ the budget.
e: The adjective 'responsible' takes 'for'.

q: This is ___ film I have ever seen.
e: Superlatives use 'the most' with long adjectives.

q: Not only is he clever, ___ he is kind.
e: 'Not only... but also' is a correlative structure.

q: The company decided to cut ___ on advertising.
e: 'Cut back on' means to reduce.

q: The negotiations broke ___ after three days.
e: 'Break down' means to fail or collapse.

q: By next year, I ___ here for ten years.
e: Future perfect shows what will be complete by a future time.

q: What does 'sick' mean?
e: 'Sick' means ill or not well.

q: The opposite of 'weak' is ___.
e: Strong is the opposite of weak.

q: I have a high ___ and I feel very hot.
e: A fever is a high body temperature caused by illness.

q: A person who teaches in a school is a ___.
e: A teacher gives lessons to students.

q: Where do students study? They go to ___.
e: Students study at school.

q: The opposite of 'easy' is ___.
e: Difficult means not easy.

q: The sky is full of ___ in the rainy season.
e: Clouds are seen in the sky, especially in the rainy season.

q: Rain is water that falls from ___.
e: Rain falls from clouds in the sky.

q: A place with many trees is a ___.
e: A forest is a large area covered with trees.

q: A person who fixes cars is a ___.
e: A mechanic repairs vehicles.

q: I get paid every month. I earn a ___.
e: A salary is the regular monthly pay for a job.

q: The opposite of 'to hire' is ___.
e: To fire means to end someone's job, the opposite of hiring.

q: I need a ___ to fly to another country.
e: A passport is an official document for travelling abroad.

q: The place where planes take off is the ___.
e: Planes take off and land at an airport.

q: A hotel room for one person is a ___ room.
e: A single room has one bed for one person.

q: Bread is made from ___.
e: Flour is ground grain used to make bread.

q: What do you drink with breakfast? Milk or ___.
e: Juice is a drink, the others are foods.

q: I am hungry. I want to ___ something.
e: When you are hungry, you want to eat.

q: A ___ is used to make calls and send texts.
e: A phone is a device for calls and messages.

q: The internet connects ___ all over the world.
e: The internet links computers and devices together.

q: To turn on a computer, you press the ___.
e: The power button starts the device.

q: My mother's sister is my ___.
e: Your mother's sister is your aunt.

q: My aunt's son is my ___.
e: A cousin is the child of your aunt or uncle.

q: A young person who is not yet an adult is a ___.
e: A child is a young person.

q: A place where you keep your money is a ___.
e: You keep and save money at a bank.

q: The price of a thing is its ___.
e: The cost is how much you pay for something.

q: The opposite of 'to buy' is ___.
e: To sell is the opposite of to buy.

q: A person who reads the news on TV is a ___.
e: A newsreader presents the news on television.

q: A paper that comes out every day with the news is a ___.
e: A newspaper is printed regularly with news.

q: What do you watch at the cinema? A ___.
e: People watch a film at the cinema.

q: Which word means 'to get better after an illness'?
e: To recover is to become well again.

q: A doctor who treats teeth is a ___.
e: A dentist looks after teeth and gums.

q: A patient in ___ condition is in great danger.
e: Critical means very serious and dangerous.

q: A medicine that stops pain is a ___.
e: A painkiller reduces or removes pain.

q: A short test to check what you know is a ___.
e: A quiz is a short set of questions to test knowledge.

q: A student who must do the same school year again ___ it.
e: To repeat a year means to do the same year again.

q: A person who gives lectures at university is a ___.
e: A lecturer teaches courses at a university.

q: To ___ a language means to learn it very well.
e: To master something is to become very skilled at it.

q: Smoke and waste that make the air dirty are ___.
e: Pollution is harmful substances in air, water or soil.

q: Cutting down too many trees is called ___.
e: Deforestation is the clearing of forests.

q: A long period with no rain is a ___.
e: A drought is a long time with little or no rain.

q: A person who is paid to do a job is an ___.
e: An employee works for an employer and is paid.

q: The person who hires workers and pays them is the ___.
e: An employer hires and pays employees.

q: To stop working for a company is to ___.
e: To resign means to leave a job by choice.

q: The opposite of 'to promote' is ___.
e: To demote means to move someone to a lower position.

q: A document that lets you enter a country is a ___.
e: A visa is permission to enter a country.

q: A person who travels for pleasure is a ___.
e: A tourist visits places for fun.

q: The place where you wait for a train is the ___.
e: You wait for a train on the platform.

q: A holiday on a big ship that visits many ports is a ___.
e: A cruise is a voyage on a large passenger ship.

q: Meat from a cow is called ___.
e: Beef comes from cows, pork from pigs.

q: A thick dish of meat and vegetables cooked slowly in liquid is a ___.
e: A stew is cooked slowly in liquid.

q: A person who cooks in a restaurant is a ___.
e: A chef is a professional cook.

q: Food that is off and smells bad is ___.
e: Rotten food has gone bad.

q: The opposite of 'to upload' is ___.
e: To download is to copy data from the internet to your device.

q: A small computer you can hold in your hand is a ___.
e: A smartphone is a mobile phone with computer features.

q: My father's parents are my ___.
e: Your father's parents are your grandparents.

q: A child's brother or sister is their ___.
e: A sibling is a brother or sister.

q: When you borrow money from a bank, you take out a ___.
e: A loan is money you borrow and pay back.

q: A reduction in the price of something is a ___.
e: A discount lowers the price.

q: A short written piece in a newspaper is an ___.
e: An article is a piece of writing in a newspaper or magazine.

q: A ___ illness lasts a long time and cannot be cured.
e: A chronic illness is long-lasting.

q: Which word means 'to protect someone from a disease with an injection'?
e: To vaccinate is to give a vaccine that prevents disease.

q: The name the doctor gives to an illness after examining you is the ___.
e: A diagnosis is the identification of an illness.

q: Which is a symptom of the flu?
e: A high temperature is a common sign of flu.

q: To ___ for a course means to register for it.
e: To enrol is to sign up formally for a course.

q: After university, students ___ with a degree.
e: To graduate means to finish studies and receive a degree.

q: A long piece of academic writing, often for a PhD, is a ___.
e: A thesis is a long research document.

q: The opposite of 'to pollute' is ___.
e: To conserve means to protect and keep something safe.

q: Animals in danger of disappearing are ___.
e: Endangered species are at risk of dying out.

q: Energy from the sun or wind is ___ energy.
e: Renewable energy comes from sources that do not run out.

q: A ___ is a formal agreement between an employer and an employee.
e: A contract sets out the terms of work.

q: A short document that lists your education and past jobs is your ___.
e: A CV summarises your education and work experience.

q: To work together with others towards one goal is to ___.
e: To collaborate means to work jointly with others.

q: A ticket that takes you to a place and back is a ___ ticket.
e: A return ticket covers the journey both ways.

q: A trip to see famous places, usually with a guide, is a ___ tour.
e: A sightseeing tour visits interesting places.

q: The place where you collect your bags at an airport is the ___.
e: Baggage claim is where you pick up your luggage after landing.

q: Food cooked in hot oil, like chips, is ___.
e: Fried food is cooked in hot oil or fat.

q: The opposite of 'raw' is ___.
e: Cooked food has been heated; raw food has not.

q: To cut vegetables into very small pieces is to ___ them.
e: To chop is to cut food into small pieces.

q: To send a file from your computer to the internet is to ___ it.
e: To upload means to send data to a server or website.

q: The part of a computer where data is stored permanently is the ___.
e: The hard drive stores files even when the power is off.

q: To put a program on your computer is to ___ it.
e: To install means to set up software so it can be used.

q: A person who looks after children for a short time while parents are out is a ___.
e: A babysitter cares for children temporarily.

q: The child of your uncle or aunt is your ___.
e: A cousin is your uncle's or aunt's child.

q: Money you save for the future is your ___.
e: Savings is money set aside for later.

q: Money you pay each month to live in a flat is ___.
e: Rent is the regular payment for using a home.

q: The extra money a bank pays you for keeping savings is ___.
e: Interest is extra money paid on savings.

q: A film or programme that shows real events and facts is a ___.
e: A documentary presents factual information.

q: A regular TV drama about the same characters and their daily lives is a ___.
e: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama.

q: A short clip that previews a new film is a ___.
e: A trailer shows a preview of a film.
